2. Suits in questions were instituted seeking a declaration that the deeds of gift dated 14th October, 1985 executed by Meherun Nessa were fraudulent and void, inasmuch as these deeds were created by resorting to forgery. The trial court dismissed title suit No. 55 of 1986 and decreed title suit No. 54 of 1986. On Appeal from the said Judgment, the court of appeal below reversed the Judgment dismissing title suit No. 55 of 1986 and decreed the same, while dismissing title suit No. 55 of 1986 decreed by the trial court. The High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 803 of 1995 against the judgment passed the title appeal No. 76 of 1991 arose out of title Suit No. 55 of 1986. A Single Bench of the High Court Division reversed the judgment of the court of appeal and restored the judgment passed in the title suit No. 55 of 1986 by judgment and order dated 28th November, 1993. It however, affirmed the judgment of the dismissal of title suit No. 54 of 1986. Thereafter, the plaintiff filed applications for rehearing of the rules. Another Single Bench of the High Court Division allowed the application with cost of Tk. 2500/- and set aside the judgment and order dated 26th November 2001. The question is whether a Single Bench of the High Court Division having co-ordinate jurisdiction can sit over the judgment of another Single Bench. 

 3. There is no dispute that the Single Bench of the High Court Division ex-parte disposed of civil revision and interfered with the findings of the court of appeal below, in respect of one suit. Another Single Bench of the High Court Division has entertained the applications for rehearing of the matters after disposal of the rules on merit. The learned judge of the Single Bench failed to notice that after the disposal of the rules on merit by another Single Bench of co-ordinate jurisdiction, it cannot sit over the matters again. After the delivery of the judgment, a Single Bench of the High Court Division becomes functus officio and it cannot re-hear the matters and sit over the judgment of another Single Bench of co-ordinate jurisdiction other than to make corrections of clerical or arithmetical mistakes in the judgments, decrees or errors arising from therein from any accidental slip or omission under section 152 of the Code of Civil Procedure in the absence of the author Judge, Besides, it can review any judgment or order if a proper application for review is filed on the ground of discovery of new and important matter or evidence which, after the exercise of due diligence could not be produced at the time when the judgment, order or decree was passed or that there was some mistake or error apparent on the face of the record or for any sufficient cause under order 47 rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 5. Mr. Mahbubey Alam, learned Counsel appearing for the respondent submits that in the previous judgment the High Court Division has palpably committed error in reversing the judgments of the court of appeal below, inasmuch as, the plaintiff has instituted three suits against two sons and one daughter on similar facts, but the court of appeal below decreed two suits, one against a son and another against the daughter but dismissed the other suit filed against another son and the High Court Division reversed the decree passed in title suit No. 55 of 1986 and affirmed the judgment of the appellate court dismissing title suit No. 54 If 1986. He further submitted that the High Court Division in the previous judgment did not notice that though Rabeya, daughter of the plaintiff did not file any revision, it has affirmed the decree passed by the lower appellate court. Therefore, it is argued that there is palpable error in the earlier judgment passed by the High Court Division and in the latter judgment this error has been detected. According to the learned Counsel, this Division may treat the applications for rehearing as one of applications for review.
